meta.shape_note: Dumbbell plan, not a rectangle. Narrow gable ends (~52 ft north, ~53.5 ft south), two projecting wing zones at 23-52 ft and 90-120 ft along the axis reaching ~63 ft, and a NARROW waist of 41-48 ft in the middle. The north end zone runs 120-143 ft along the axis: 23 ft deep and 51-53 ft wide. That is the pocket the suite sits in.
meta.sources: Footprint cross-checked against 5 independent datasets: Harvard ArcGIS Facilities3D, Cambridge GIS BASEMAP_Buildings (highest fidelity, 52 vertices), MassGIS Building Structures 2-D (2011 roofprint), OpenStreetMap way 29824449, Microsoft GlobalMLBuildingFootprints. Heights and areas from Cambridge GIS and the Cambridge BEUDO energy-disclosure dataset. Earlier figures of 54 x 151 ft were both wrong: 54 was one facade edge, 151 was the rotation-inflated bounding box.

primary_source_1875.citation: The Harvard Book, Vaille & Clark eds., 1875, vol. 1, pp. 135-136
primary_source_1875.stair_halls_position: central, top-lit by lanterns above the roof
primary_source_1875.main_entrance: west front, two arches into a 21 x 25 ft marble-paved loggia
primary_source_1875.service: coal lift closet with a public sink off each stair hall on every story
primary_source_1875.daylighting: all studies except the 16 in the central part, and all double bedrooms, have windows in two directions; NO ROOMS RECEIVE AN EXCLUSIVELY NORTH LIGHT
primary_source_1875.corroboration: The Harvard Register vol III no 3, March 1881, pp 142-143: "From each hall open twenty-seven studies"

renovations.1962: gut remodel of all five floors; new suite partitions, new toilet rooms, stair hall replaced, common room built; capacity 71 to 118; rooms completely renumbered (PIRC 1962-010)
renovations.1992-93: second gut renovation; north stair, south stair with new hydraulic elevator, east entrance made accessible; capacity 150 (PIRC HRE 1991-003)

room_numbering.pre_1962: two vertical entries, one continuous 1-55 sequence, floor-independent. South entry 12-27, North 33-55 (Crimson, 12 Sept 1951)
room_numbering.post_1962: INFERRED, tightly constrained: first digit = floor = entryway, second digit runs south to north along the corridor
room_numbering.weld_15: fifth suite on the first floor, north half of the corridor; entryway Weld 1
